posts.title: Reed Waller, RIP
posts.description: In 1986, the arrest and subsequent conviction of a comic shop manager for selling Reed Waller’s Omaha the Cat Dancer led to the creation of the Comic Book Legal Defense Fund. This image is from A Benefit Portfolio in Defense of the First Amendment, the historic Denis Kitchen fundraiser that launched the CBLDF Thanks, Reed, for fighting the good fight.

posts.title: CBLDF Comic-Con Welcome Party Returns to San Diego!
posts.description: JULY 15, 2026 (PORTLAND, OR) — The Comic Book Legal Defense Fund (CBLDF), with support from Marquee sponsors Mad Cave Studios and Ignition Press , and Gold tier sponsor GlobalComix , and and Silver tier sponsors Kickstarter , and CGC , will once again welcome the comics community to its Annual San Diego Comic-Con Welcome Party on Thursday, July 23, 2026, from 8:00 PM to 12 AM , at The Westgate Hotel (1055 Second Ave., San Diego, CA). The annual fundraiser brings together creators, publishers, retailers, media, and fans for an evening celebrating comics while raising critical funds to defend the freedom to read. For decades, the Comic Book Legal Defense Fund has stood at the forefront of protecting free expression in comics, providing legal assistance, education, and advocacy in response to censorship efforts affecting comic books, graphic novels, manga, and the people who create, sell, teach, and read them. posts.title: A Legal Look at the Book Ban Bill, HR 7661
posts.description: HR 7661 is an unconstitutional campaign-year ploy that even its sponsors don’t think will pass. Its real aim: to get free press as the defenders of children while making it look like our agenda is to sexualize kids in schools. Should we be playing their game? What is HR 7661? On February 24th, a small group of Republicans in the House of Representatives introduced House Bill 7661 , the so-called Stop the Sexualization of Children Act. The title is an all too common rhetorical trick, signaling from the outset that this bill is less about solving real problems than scoring a cheap political point against anyone who dares to oppose it.
